<!-- audience-switcher:end -->

automated tests
:   Checks, run on request by the developers, that confirm the model still behaves as expected.

callsign
:   The radio name of a vehicle on duty, such as H70 (a helicopter) or CC72 (a car).

crew group (callsign group)
:   Vehicles that share one crew, such as helicopter H70 and car CC70; only one can be out at a time.

critical care (CC)
:   The highest level of pre-hospital care the service provides; one of the three care categories in the model.

enhanced care (EC)
:   A level of care above standard ambulance care but below critical care.

helicopter benefit
:   Whether a patient would gain from a helicopter rather than a car, for example for speed or access.

historical baseline
:   Model results using the rotas that actually ran in the past, used to check the model against reality.

hosted site
:   A copy of the web app running on an outside service, reachable in a browser without installing anything.

learned patterns (fitted distributions)
:   Mathematical descriptions of past data, such as how long time on scene usually takes, which the model draws from.

missed job
:   A call for which no air ambulance vehicle was free and suitable at the time, so none was sent.

open-source licence
:   The terms under which the code can be used and changed; this project uses GPL-3.0.

parameter template
:   An Excel workbook the user fills in to describe a scenario and upload to the web app.

random seed
:   A starting number that fixes the random chances, so the same seed and settings give the same results again.

regular job (REG)
:   A job not identified as needing critical or enhanced care.

rota
:   The table of which vehicles are on shift at which hours, with separate summer and winter hours.

run (replication)
:   One complete play-through of the simulated period. The model does many runs, each with different random chances, and averages them.

scenario
:   A set of settings (rota, fleet, servicing, demand) to test.

servicing
:   Planned maintenance that takes an aircraft out of use for several weeks.

short-notice (ad hoc) unavailability
:   Times a helicopter cannot fly although on shift, for example due to weather or crew issues.

simulation
:   A computer model that imitates a real service over time, so that changes can be tried out safely.

the call simulator
:   The part that creates each day's made-up calls and patients and plays out each job step by step.

the dispatch rules
:   The part that decides which vehicle, if any, goes to each call.

the fleet and rota model
:   The part that represents each helicopter and car, its shift hours and its servicing dates.

the historical data preparer
:   An occasional, separate step that turns real job records into the patterns and summaries the model uses. 

the pattern sampler
:   The part that holds patterns learned from past jobs and draws realistic values from them.

the results and comparison tool
:   The part that turns run records into figures and charts and compares them with real past performance.

the run manager
:   The part that repeats the model many times with different random chances and combines the results.

the web app
:   The set of web pages where users choose a scenario, run the model and view the results.

utilisation
:   The share of a vehicle's on-shift hours spent on jobs.
